While the Dolphin 24L can physically mount on front racks, we recommend them primarily for rear use due to their larger size (24L per bag). The weight and volume work best on rear racks for balanced handling. For front loading, consider the Dolphin 16L, which is specifically designed for front or rear use and provides better front-end handling with its moderate capacity. For fully loaded touring, pair Dolphin 16L on your front rack (32L total) with Dolphin 24L on your rear rack (48L total) for a complete 80L system. This front/rear combination provides excellent weight distribution, keeps your bike balanced and stable, and offers organized storage for extended adventures. The complete kit handles everything from lightweight summer touring to winter expeditions with bulky gear.

How do you combine the advantages of multiple functional zippered pockets with total waterproofness? We achieved the absolute best of both worlds by adding a 100% waterproof liner inside the whole main compartment of the GT-54. The liner is made of lightweight, fully waterproof, polyurethane-coated nylon. The zippers on the liner allow for full frontal access to the main compartment in the same fashion as the front panel of the bag itself. While the GT-54 can physically hold substantial weight, we recommend keeping loads reasonable for comfortable riding and bike component longevity. Most expedition cyclists load 15-20 lbs (7-9 kg) per pannier, totaling 30-40 lbs (14-18 kg) for the pair. The bags structurally handle more, but excessive weight affects bike handling and component wear. Proper weight distribution between front and rear panniers (if running front bags) is more important than maximum weight capacity. Yes, the GT-54's internal aluminum frame is removable if you want to reduce weight for ultralight touring or bikepacking-style trips. Similarly, the rigid UHMWPE plastic panel can be trimmed or removed by the customer. Removing these components saves 200-400g per pannier but reduces structural support‚ the bags will sag more when loaded and be harder to pack efficiently. Most touring cyclists keep the frame/panel for the organizational benefits, but weight-conscious riders can customize.

The Wellington is water-resistant, not fully waterproof. The recycled XPac fabric repels rain, splashes, and light-to-moderate precipitation effectively, protecting your gear during typical urban cycling conditions. For heavy downpours or all-day rain, we recommend Arkel's fully waterproof bags like the Signature series. The Wellington's water-resistance is designed to handle the unpredictable weather of daily commuting without the weight and bulk of fully waterproof construction. Yes! The Wellington's padded shoulder strap is designed to swap between left and right-shoulder carry, so you can choose your preferred side or alternate to distribute weight evenly. The adjustable third-point stabilizer strap keeps the bag secure against your body while cycling, preventing bounce and sway regardless of which shoulder you choose. This versatility makes the Wellington comfortable for all-day wear.
